description: An edited draft under a new approval is different content going out and gets a new key.
why_it_exists: The WF4 outbound delivery key was once derived with $now in the basis, so a second attempt at the same approved delivery produced a different send_key and a different communication_id. An uncertain send result (a timeout after the message had actually gone) therefore resolved to a brand new row on retry, and the same letter could be sent to an insurer twice with no duplicate detectable anywhere in the register. Different content under a new approval must not reuse the delivery identity of the superseded draft, or the edited letter would be suppressed as a duplicate of the original.

expect.note: The original oracle hashes were computed by a separate Python FNV-1a implementation over the REAL recipient address. That address has been replaced by a same-length synthetic address, so the expected hash must be regenerated from this input with an independent FNV-1a implementation before this assertion means anything. Do not copy the value the JavaScript under test produces. The original assertion was send_key === "SND-1d1361c3".

assertions: send_key differs from both the first send and the duplicate-approval key
send_key equals "SND-" + the independently computed FNV-1a of "apr=APR-003 act=ACT-001 draft=DFT-002 chan=GMAIL to=insurerclaims01@example.com"
